previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, alcohol use disorder, and tobacco use, was admitted for alcohol detoxification and hypoxemia. He presented with shortness of breath and a history of recent alcohol use, and was found to have worsening bronchial infiltration on chest X-ray suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with clindamycin, azithromycin, prednisone, and albuterol for pneumonia and COPD exacerbation, and managed for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam, which was tapered as symptoms improved. His oxygen levels stabilized, and he was discharged to extended care with a plan to continue medications and pursue rehabilitation. He expressed a strong desire to remain sober and engage in recovery support, and was given follow-up instructions for PFTs and outpatient workup of atypical white blood cells noted on differential.

Brief Hospital Course:
PATIENT LEFT AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE

The patient is a ___ year old male with a history of alcohol 
abuse, asplenia s/p MVA, chronic pain who presents with 
continued cough and alcohol intoxication and left AMA after 
achieving sobriety.

  
# Alcohol Abuse/Dependence with Intoxication and Withdrawal: Has 
long history of alcohol use with repeated hospitalizations for 
intoxication. Has h/o DTs and seizures. Patient intoxicated and 
may be in early withdrawal given mild tremors but difficult to 
assess as patient is uncooperative. Serum alcohol level of 277. 
Last drink was ___ at 8am. Patient refusing care and 
attempting to leave AMA while intoxicated overnight from 
___ and given diazepam 10mg Q3H initially and then 
switched to Q2H overnight. Security was called multiple times to 
escort patient back into his room while grossly intoxicated: 
slurry speech, disorganized, making threatening comments and 
gestures towards staff. Multivitamin, folate and PO thiamine (IV 
access refused and thus gave oral thiamine) given. Section 35 
paperwork was pending at time of patient being lucid on ___ 
morning. As he was A&Ox3 and not in active withdrawal, he was 
able to understand the risks of leaving against medical advice.

.  
# Cough/Hypoxia: Was being treated for CAP and COPD exacerbation 
during previous admission and did not complete steroid and abx 
course. Here with cough and hypoxia but afebrile and without 
leukocytosis and thus unlikely pneumonia. CXR from ___ suggests 
possible infectious infiltrate. Patient did not fit SIRS 
criteria and lactate mildly elevated to 2.1. Patient refused 
nebs and physical exam.
Medical team wanted to continue community acquired pneumonia and 
COPD flare treatment which was not finished on recent 
hospitalization but pt refused. No documented fevers during 
brief admission.

.
#Chest pain: patient complaining of chest tightness in setting 
of intoxication/possible withdrawal upon coming to floor. 
Patient inconsistent, disorganized and confused. Refusing ECG at 
this time. Denies SOB. No cardiac history. +HTN but no DM, 
stroke or HLD history. Normotensive and not tachycardic. Patient 
refused 12 lead ECG. Troponin and MB negative and thus less 
likely ACS. Patient left AMA without complaining of chest pain.
  
# Hypertension: Per patient, he has not been taking his 
Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO BID   

# Chronic Pain: He reports chronic pain from his injuries in 
___, and is on Methadone 10 mg PO TID at baseline which he has 
not been taking since d/c from this hospital. Percocet was not 
on recent discharge med list.
.  
#Atypicals on Differential: Has history of atypical cells on 
diff as well as high eosinophil fraction. Likely related to 
chronic alcohol abuse affecting bone marrow.
